description: Recommend the best current-generation LLM for a coding task category, ranked by the same benchmark/capability data the other tools expose (SWE-bench Pro/Verified, Vibe Code Bench (Vals AI, OpenHands harness), Terminal-Bench 4.0 (Vals AI, Mini-SWE-agent harness), or a qualitative capability-rating fallback for categories no benchmark covers well, such as test-gen and library-aware-feature-work). library-aware-feature-work currently ranks on the same coding capability rating as test-gen, so the two rankings match until a scored board covers current models. Recommendation only — this never calls a provider or touches an API key; pass the returned model_id to your own inference call. Optionally restrict to specific providers (e.g. the ones you have keys for). Coverage is honestly reported: some category/provider combinations currently have zero ranked models because the underlying benchmark hasn't been sourced for that model yet (see 'unscored') or the benchmark itself is barely tracked industry-wide — this tool never fabricates a ranking to fill the gap. An empty ranking carries notice.code 'no_ranked_models' saying why. new-code-generation and terminal-cli are ranked in tie bands: models whose scores are within each other's measurement error (95%) and within 3 points of the band's top model are treated as tied and listed cheapest first, and each carries 'band' (1 = top). A model with no published standard error ties only an exact score. A ranked model whose provider has announced a shutdown carries 'shutdown_date'; after that date it isn't ranked. A model with no current standard per-token input price isn't ranked, whatever its status. Preview models are left out unless include_preview is true. If the question names one of the specific tracked benchmarks — SWE-bench Pro, SWE-bench Verified, Vibe Code Bench, Terminal-Bench 4.0 — do NOT use this tool to answer it: this tool's score is a per-category choice among several candidate benchmarks, not that benchmark's raw score (e.g. bug-fix and refactor prefer SWE-bench Pro over SWE-bench Verified whenever a model has both, so a model's rank here can sit well below where its named-benchmark score alone would place it). Use modelglass_list_models or modelglass_get_model instead — both return each tracked benchmark's raw score directly, with no category substitution.

category.description: The kind of coding task to route: bug-fix, new-code-generation, terminal-cli, library-aware-feature-work, refactor, test-gen, doc-gen, chat-explain, or autocomplete.

include_preview.description: Include models whose status is preview (default false). Preview models can change or be withdrawn without notice, so they aren't recommended unless you ask for them.

providers.description: Optional list of provider slugs to restrict the recommendation to (e.g. the caller's own configured providers). A canonical company id (e.g. 'google', 'openai', 'together') expands to that company's offerings across every vertical it spans. Omit to rank across every provider.

name: modelglass_route_task

excluded.description: Had signal but excluded for a stated reason (e.g. wrong Terminal-Bench harness).

notice.description: Present only when the ranking needs a caveat. 'inputs_frozen': this category's ranking benchmarks no longer score new models, so newer models are under 'unscored', not ranked lower. 'no_ranked_models': nothing ranked, because no currently priced model in this selection has a score or rating this category uses; inputs_last_updated is then the date of the data checked. Tolerate codes you don't recognise.

band.description: Tie band, 1 = top. Set for new-code-generation and terminal-cli: models in one band are tied within measurement error and 3 points, and listed cheapest first.

shutdown_date.description: Set when the provider has announced a shutdown: the date (YYYY-MM-DD, provider's calendar) from which the model is no longer priced or recommended. Absent otherwise.

unscored.description: No signal at all for this category.
